title: One-Stop Strategy
statement:
Tyres get slower every lap. On a set of tyres, the **k-th lap** of the stint takes `B + D × (k − 1)` milliseconds.

The race has `L` laps. The team can either **not stop at all**, or make **exactly one** pit stop at the end of lap `p` (1 ≤ p ≤ L − 1), which costs `P` milliseconds and gives fresh tyres for lap `p + 1`.

Print the minimum total race time and the best stop lap. Print `0` as the lap if not stopping is best. If several options give the same minimum time, choose **no stop** if possible, otherwise the **smallest** `p`.
input_format: One line with four integers `L B D P`.
output_format: Two integers: the minimum race time and the stop lap.

examples.explanation: No stop: 945000. Stop after lap 5: 460000 + 20000 + 460000 = 940000, which is the best.
The tyres degrade too slowly; stopping never pays off (no stop = 922500).

starter_code:
L, B, D, P = map(int, input().split())

# your code here
notes: Python integers never overflow, but watch the running time: L can be 200000.
